name: Nifty Outfit Nook API
status: 33a: try-on pictures on POST /v1/try-on (the faceless photo and garment photos in, one dressed picture out, made in the background and fetched with the same Idempotency-Key) (30c: purchases verified on the server; 30b: picture credits; 24d: support; 27a: the cloud stylist); 31: feedback notes can carry an approved device-health summary (counts of crashes, hangs and similar, no stacks or text)
notes: This file is the single source of truth for the app-to-backend API. The backend tests and the app's contract tests both read it and the golden examples next to it.
The app never names an AI provider, model or prompt. Later endpoints ask the backend to do a job (for example to style); the backend chooses the provider.
Every JSON body is UTF-8, at most limits.maxBodyBytes. Unknown fields in a request are rejected. Clients ignore unknown fields in a response and treat an unknown error code by its HTTP status.

Paid endpoints (cost "paid") need an Idempotency-Key header and an App Attest assertion. A retry with the same key and the same body never runs or counts twice: it gets the first answer back. The same key with a different body is idempotency_conflict.

Limits live on the server and the app can't change them: a per-user rate limit (rate_limited), daily and 30-day allowances per category (quota_exceeded, with resetAt), and per-feature and per-provider switches and spending ceilings (feature_paused). GET /v1/usage shows what is left without naming amounts of money.

Authorization: every endpoint acts only on the caller's own account, taken from the verified token. No request names an account, a row or another user's ID, so there is nothing to point at someone else's data. An account being deleted gets forbidden on every endpoint except the deletion ones.

Account deletion (24c): POST /v1/account/deletion needs a fresh Sign in with Apple authorization code (re-authentication, and what the backend needs to revoke the Apple sign-in link). It answers 202 with the deletion's ID and steps; repeating it returns the same deletion and carries on. Once the account is gone the token stops working, so the status endpoint takes the deletion ID instead of a token. The ID is random and the status names no person.

Stylist (27a): POST /v1/style sends a bounded snapshot of the pieces she can use (IDs and plain descriptors, never photos, notes, brands, sizes or her name) and returns looks that reference only those IDs. The backend chooses the provider and model from its own configuration and checks every answer before it is returned. consentVersion names the consent text she agreed to; when it doesn't cover the backend's current provider the answer is consent_required and nothing is sent.

Stylist results: kind complete (three versions), partial (fewer, with each missing version and why), insufficient (no outfit can be made from these pieces; nothing counted), or answer (mode ask). fromCache is true when an identical request from the same account in the last 24 hours was answered again without asking the provider; such an answer doesn't count against an allowance.

Support (24d): POST /v1/feedback sends one private note to the support queue. It needs a token but not App Attest, on purpose: support has to work on a device that can't attest, and it costs nothing. It is limited per account (a token bucket, a daily count and a daily count of screenshots) and for all accounts together; over a limit is rate_limited, or unavailable for the all-accounts limit and when Jose closes intake. submissionId makes a resend safe: the same submissionId from the same account gets the same ticket back and stores nothing twice. An optional screenshot (JPEG or PNG, base64) has its metadata (EXIF, GPS, text and thumbnail chunks) removed by the backend, whatever the app did first; anything else is invalid_request. Diagnostics and closetCounts are included only when the person turned them on, and the app shows exactly these values before sending.

Picture credits (30b): after a StoreKit purchase of a credit pack the app sends the transaction's signed JWS to POST /v1/credits/claim, and finishes the transaction only after a 200. The backend reads the transaction ID and product ID from the JWS, never from the app, credits the pack's size from its own product list, and credits each transaction ID once: a repeat from the same account gets the first answer with replayed true, and a transaction already credited to another account is forbidden. Until 30c checks Apple's signature and the App Store Server API, crediting is mocked and only on when the backend's NOOK_CREDITS_MODE is mock; otherwise the endpoint is unavailable and the app keeps the transaction to try again. Credits never expire. GET /v1/usage shows the balance.

30c, purchases: every signed transaction the app sends (POST /v1/credits/claim, POST /v1/entitlements/claim) is verified on the server against Apple's certificates before anything is credited or linked. The app's X-Nook-Entitlement-Hint is never used to authorize anything. Styling access comes from Apple's records only: the subscription (renewals, expiry, grace period, refunds and Family Sharing revocations arrive through App Store Server Notifications, which aren't part of this contract) or the complimentary unlock. Pass user.appAccountToken to StoreKit with every purchase (Product.PurchaseOption.appAccountToken) so Apple's notifications can be matched to the account.

Try-on (33a): POST /v1/try-on sends only the faceless photo (her head already masked with flat grey on the phone and her room replaced with a plain studio backdrop) and the photos of the pieces to put on her, with category and kind for each. Nothing else of hers may be sent: no face, no room, no names, notes or measurements. The backend writes the picture instruction itself from the categories and kinds. consentVersion is the try-on consent text she agreed to; if it doesn't cover the service the backend would send the photos to, the answer is consent_required and nothing is sent or counted. The first POST checks everything, admits and counts the action, starts the picture and answers 409 action_in_progress with Retry-After 5 and the message "Your picture is being made.". The app then asks again with the same Idempotency-Key and the SAME body (byte for byte, or it is idempotency_conflict) after Retry-After, until it gets 200 with the dressed picture or an error. An attempt that failed is started once more by the next ask (at most two attempts, the second counted again only if it works); after that the answer is 503 unavailable "This action didn't work. Start a new one.". A picture can take a few minutes; the action's lease is 6 minutes, after which the outcome is checked by hand (409 with Retry-After 60). The backend keeps the photos only sealed and only while the picture is made: the inputs are deleted as soon as the picture service answers, and the result is kept sealed for at most 30 minutes, and 2 minutes after it was first delivered. After that the same key gets 503 unavailable "That picture is no longer kept. Make a new one.". The first 200 has replayed false; later ones replayed true. The picture service may keep what it receives and use it to improve its models, which the consent text must say.

feedback.note: Only this endpoint accepts a body larger than limits.maxBodyBytes. The numbers are the backend's starting settings and are enforced on the server; the app never relies on them.

tryOn.note: POST /v1/try-on only. Sizes are of the decoded image bytes, checked on the server; the body as a whole stays under maxBodyBytes. Neither side of her photo may pass personMaxPixelsPerSide, nor either side of a piece's photo garmentMaxPixelsPerSide (the app sends at most 1280 and 768); a bigger one is invalid_request with the message "The photo is too large in pixels. Its longest side can be 2048 pixels." (or "The piece's photo ...1024 pixels."), and nothing is counted. At least one garment, each id once. Each image must really be the JPEG or PNG its contentType says; the backend removes metadata (EXIF, GPS, text chunks) whatever the app did first.

auth.token: A Clerk session token minted from the JWT template named "convex" (aud "convex"). The backend takes the user only from the verified token, never from a body or query field.
auth.onUnauthorized: On any 401 the client gets a fresh token once and retries the request once. A second 401 means signed out.

request.Authorization: Bearer <token>, on every endpoint whose auth is "required".
request.Content-Type: application/json, on every request that has a body.
request.Idempotency-Key: On every paid endpoint: 16 to 64 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -, new for each new action and reused for every retry of it. Kept at least 24 hours.
request.X-Nook-Attest-Key: On every paid endpoint: the App Attest key ID (base64) registered with POST /v1/attest/key.
request.X-Nook-Assertion: On every paid endpoint: base64 of the App Attest assertion (CBOR, as DCAppAttestService.generateAssertion returns it) over SHA-256 of the client data in attestation.clientData.
request.X-Nook-Entitlement-Hint: Optional, on paid endpoints (30a): what StoreKit on the phone says about her styling access, one of none, trial, active, grace, billing-retry, expired, revoked, or complimentary (30b: the complimentary unlock from an offer code). A hint only: the backend never admits or refuses anything because of it. Since 30c the backend checks its own record of Apple's verified transactions and notifications.

response.Content-Type: application/json on every response, errors included.
response.X-Request-Id: An opaque ID on every response, for support. Also in error bodies as requestId.
response.Retry-After: Whole seconds. Always on 429; on 503 when the backend knows how long.

endpoints.summary: Called after every sign-in. Creates the account's pseudonymous user ID the first time, records a sign-in audit event, and returns who the token belongs to.
Who am I. Reads only; never creates the account.
What is left of each allowance, when it next frees up, and whether each paid feature is on. Names no amounts of money and no provider.
A one-time challenge for registering an App Attest key. Expires after 5 minutes.
Registers this install's App Attest key with its attestation over a challenge from POST /v1/attest/challenge.

The cloud stylist (27a). Runs the full admission path (attestation, idempotency, rate limit, allowance, switches, cost reservation), then the server's stylist. mode full makes one outfit in up to three versions; mode ask answers a question about a look, with the earlier turns of that conversation.

One try-on picture (33a). The request carries the faceless photo of her on a plain studio backdrop (her head already a flat grey shape, made on the phone) and the photos of the pieces to put on her. It runs the full admission path (attestation, idempotency, consent, rate limit, one action at a time, allowance or a picture credit, switches, cost reservation), then the picture is made in the background: the first request answers 409 action_in_progress and the app asks again with the same Idempotency-Key and the same body until it gets 200 with the dressed picture, or an error.

Deletes the caller's account: every record the backend keeps for it, the Apple sign-in link and the sign-in account itself, and cancels pending paid work. Needs a fresh Sign in with Apple authorization code. Safe to repeat: the same deletion comes back and carries on from where it stopped. Steps the backend couldn't finish are retried on its own.
How a deletion is going, by its ID. Needs no token, because the account and its token may already be gone. Unknown IDs are not_found.

Sends one private note to the support queue, with an optional reply address, an optional screenshot and, only if the person turned them on, app details and closet counts. 202 with a ticket reference. Safe to repeat with the same submissionId. No App Attest, on purpose.

Credits a picture-credit pack bought with StoreKit (30b). The body is the transaction's signed JWS; since 30c the backend verifies Apple's signature, bundle and environment, then takes the transaction and product from it and credits each transaction once. A refunded purchase is forbidden. Safe to repeat. No App Attest: the signed transaction is the proof, and it costs nothing.

30c: links the styling subscription or the complimentary unlock to this account and answers with the server's view of styling access. The body is the transaction's signed JWS (Transaction.jwsRepresentation, from a purchase, a redeemed offer code, a restore or currentEntitlements); the backend verifies Apple's signature, bundle and environment. Safe to repeat. A purchase another account already claimed, or bought with another account's appAccountToken, is forbidden. No App Attest: the signed transaction is the proof, and it costs nothing.

errors.meaning: The body isn't valid JSON, doesn't match the schema, or has an unknown field.
No token, or a token that doesn't verify (wrong issuer, audience or signature).
The token was valid but has expired. Refresh and retry once.
Signed in, but not allowed, for example because the account is being deleted. Don't retry.
The App Attest assertion is missing, from an unknown key, or doesn't verify. Register a key again (attestation section), then retry once.
Her consent (consentVersion) doesn't cover where the backend would send this request. Nothing was sent or counted. Ask her again with the current consent text.

30c: styling access is needed and the server's record of Apple's purchases shows none (try-on: and no picture credits either). Nothing was sent or counted. feature says which. Offer styling access (or picture packs, for try-on); after a purchase or restore, send the transaction to POST /v1/entitlements/claim, then retry.
No such endpoint in this version, or no deletion with that ID.
The token is valid but POST /v1/session hasn't run for it yet.
The endpoint exists but not with this method.
This Idempotency-Key was already used for a different request. Make a new key for a new action.
This action, or another paid action of this account, is still running, or its outcome is being checked. Wait Retry-After seconds; never send it again with a new key.
This API version is no longer served. The app must be updated.
The body is larger than limits.maxBodyBytes.
A body was sent without Content-Type: application/json.
Too many requests. Wait Retry-After seconds.
An allowance is used up. category says which; resetAt says when the next one frees up, and Retry-After the seconds until then. Don't retry before.
The backend failed. Safe to retry a read with backoff.
Switched off or overloaded. Retry later, after Retry-After when present.
This paid feature is switched off on the server, or its spending ceiling is reached. feature says which. Everything else keeps working. Retry-After when the backend knows.

planned.33a: Built (see notes). Still to come: the job with up to three child pictures (PRD 9.2.4) and a backup picture service with its own consent text.

attestation.clientData:
nook-assert-v1
<METHOD>
<PATH>
<Idempotency-Key>
<lowercase hex SHA-256 of the exact body bytes>
attestation.challengeHash: POST /v1/attest/key: DCAppAttestService.attestKey is called with clientDataHash = SHA-256 of the challenge string's UTF-8 bytes. The backend's mock mode (local and dev only) takes a stand-in attestation instead: base64 of JSON {fmt: "nook-mock-v1", publicKey: base64 of the raw P-256 key, clientDataHash: base64, appId}.
attestation.counter: Each assertion's counter must be higher than the last one the backend accepted for that key. A replayed assertion fails.
attestation.onFailure: attestation_required (403): register a new key with a fresh challenge, then retry once. Simulators and devices that can't attest get no paid access.

deletion.steps: signInWithApple: the Apple sign-in link is revoked with the authorization code sent in the request (it works once, for a few minutes, so a failed revocation needs a new request with a new code, or she removes the app in Settings > Apple Account > Sign in with Apple). serverData: every record the backend keeps for the account is deleted, and paid work still running is cancelled (its result is thrown away). account: the sign-in account is deleted, which ends every session.
deletion.states: done; pending (the backend is still working on it, or retrying on its own); failed (it can't finish without her: only signInWithApple, see above). The deletion is completed when serverData and account are done.
deletion.retained: After deletion the backend keeps no personal data. It keeps: the deletion record (the deletion ID, the pseudonymous user ID and the dates, for 35 days, so a backup restored in that time can't bring the account back), counts of recent paid use under a keyed hash for 31 days (so deleting can't reset an allowance), and an audit line with the event and time only. Spending totals per day and month never named an account.
